classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish functions from other relations before applying the horizontal line test across twelve contrasting graphs.

content.prompt: Determine whether each relation is a function. If it is, decide whether it is one-to-one and hence has an inverse function.

spec.description: Increasing straight line through the origin, arrows at both ends, labelled axes without numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Schematic positive slope; drawing coordinates do not assert a numerical slope or axis scale.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; one-to-one; has an inverse function.
answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the graph at most once, so it is a function. Every horizontal line also meets it at most once, so it is one-to-one and has an inverse function.

spec.description: Decreasing cubic-shaped curve through the origin with a horizontal tangent there and arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Schematic strictly decreasing curve; no equation or numerical scale is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; one-to-one; has an inverse function.
answer.worked: The graph passes the vertical line test. Although it flattens at the origin, each horizontal line meets it at most once. It is one-to-one and has an inverse function.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down root-shaped curve starting on the positive horizontal axis, without an endpoint marker, and continuing rightwards.
spec.mathematics: Positive horizontal displacement retained schematically; its numerical value is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; one-to-one; has an inverse function.
answer.worked: Every vertical and horizontal line meets the graph at most once. It is a one-to-one function and therefore has an inverse function.

spec.description: Horizontal line at y=1 with arrows at both ends and the value 1 beside the vertical axis.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; not one-to-one; no inverse function.
answer.worked: The graph passes the vertical line test, so it is a function. The horizontal line $y=1$ coincides with the graph and contains many points. It fails the horizontal line test, so it has no inverse function.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex at the origin and arrows at both upper ends.
spec.mathematics: Parabolic symmetry about the vertical axis; no numerical coefficient or scale is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; not one-to-one; no inverse function.
answer.worked: The graph passes the vertical line test. Horizontal lines above the vertex meet both branches, so it fails the horizontal line test. It is not one-to-one and has no inverse function on the domain shown.

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle with filled endpoints at (-1,0) and (1,0) and numerical horizontal-axis labels -1, 0 and 1.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.short: Function; not one-to-one; no inverse function.
answer.worked: Each vertical line meets the upper semicircle at most once, so it is a function. A horizontal line between $y=0$ and $y=1$ meets it twice. It is not one-to-one and has no inverse function on the domain shown.

spec.description: Left unit semicircle with filled endpoints (0,1) and (0,-1), labelled on the vertical axis.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: A vertical line through the interior of the left semicircle meets it twice. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.

spec.description: Vertical line at x=2, arrows at both ends, numerical label at its horizontal-axis intercept.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=2$ contains many points of the relation. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.

spec.description: Right-opening sideways parabola with vertex at the origin and arrows on both rightward branches.
spec.mathematics: Both branches retained with symmetry about the horizontal axis; no numerical coefficient or scale is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: A vertical line to the right of the origin meets both branches. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.

spec.description: Unfilled circle centred at (2,1), radius 2, with source numerical labels and dashed horizontal guides to its upper and lower extremes.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: For example, the vertical line $x=2$ meets the circle at $(2,3)$ and $(2,-1)$. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.

spec.description: Two outward-opening branches symmetric about both axes, with four continuation arrows and source labels -2 and 2 near the horizontal-axis vertices; no asymptotes or anchoring ticks.
spec.mathematics: Schematic branches only. The source labels are retained without asserting a complete equation or additional parameters.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: A vertical line cutting either branch away from its vertex meets it twice. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.

spec.description: Closed unfilled diamond centred at the origin, four vertices on the coordinate axes and no numerical labels.
spec.mathematics: Schematic axis-symmetric polygon; drawing coordinates do not assert numerical vertex values.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied classification in the question figure.

answer.worked: The vertical axis meets the diamond at its upper and lower vertices. It fails the vertical line test, so classification as a one-to-one function does not apply.
